base_method_text.title: Diffusion Model-Augmented Behavioral Cloning
base_method_text.summary:
Imitation learning addresses the challenge of learning by observing an
expert's demonstrations without access to reward signals from environments.
Most existing imitation learning methods that do not require interacting with
environments either model the expert distribution as the conditional
probability p(a|s) (e.g., behavioral cloning, BC) or the joint probability p(s,
a). Despite the simplicity of modeling the conditional probability with BC, it
usually struggles with generalization. While modeling the joint probability can
improve generalization performance, the inference procedure is often
time-consuming, and the model can suffer from manifold overfitting. This work
proposes an imitation learning framework that benefits from modeling both the
conditional and joint probability of the expert distribution. Our proposed
Diffusion Model-Augmented Behavioral Cloning (DBC) employs a diffusion model
trained to model expert behaviors and learns a policy to optimize both the BC
loss (conditional) and our proposed diffusion model loss (joint). DBC
outperforms baselines in various continuous control tasks in navigation, robot
arm manipulation, dexterous manipulation, and locomotion. We design additional
experiments to verify the limitations of modeling either the conditional
probability or the joint probability of the expert distribution, as well as
compare different generative models. Ablation studies justify the effectiveness
of our design choices.
base_method_text.main_contributions: The paper introduces Diffusion Model-Augmented Behavioral Cloning (DBC), a novel imitation learning framework that combines the benefits of modeling both the conditional probability p(a|s) and the joint probability p(s, a) of expert behaviors. DBC uses a diffusion model to capture the joint distribution of expert state-action pairs and trains a policy to optimize both the behavioral cloning (BC) loss and a diffusion model loss. This approach aims to improve generalization and efficiency compared to existing imitation learning methods.
base_method_text.methodology: The core methodology involves training a diffusion model to estimate the likelihood of state-action pairs from an expert dataset. This diffusion model then guides policy learning by optimizing a combined loss function. The loss function includes the standard behavioral cloning (BC) loss, which models the conditional probability p(a|s), and a diffusion model loss, which leverages the diffusion model's estimate of the joint probability p(s, a). The diffusion model is based on Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models (DDPMs).
base_method_text.experimental_setup: The proposed DBC framework was evaluated on various continuous control tasks, including navigation (MAZE), robot arm manipulation (FETCH PICK), dexterous manipulation (HAND ROTATE), and locomotion (CHEETAH, WALKER, ANTREACH). The performance was compared against baselines like Behavioral Cloning (BC), Implicit BC (IBC), and Diffusion Policy. The evaluation metrics included success rate and return. The experiments also included ablation studies to justify design choices and generalization experiments by injecting noise into initial states and goal locations.
base_method_text.limitations: The proposed framework is designed to learn from expert trajectories without interacting with the environment, which means it cannot learn from agent trajectories. Additionally, the framework inherits any biases present in the expert demonstrations, which could lead to sub-optimal, unsafe, or discriminatory behaviors.
base_method_text.future_research_directions: Future research directions include extending the method to incorporate agent data, which could allow for improvement when interacting with the environment is possible. Addressing and mitigating the biases inherited from expert demonstrators is also a crucial area for future work.

add_method_texts.title: FiT: Flexible Vision Transformer for Diffusion Model
add_method_texts.summary:
Nature is infinitely resolution-free. In the context of this reality,
existing diffusion models, such as Diffusion Transformers, often face
challenges when processing image resolutions outside of their trained domain.
To overcome this limitation, we present the Flexible Vision Transformer (FiT),
a transformer architecture specifically designed for generating images with
unrestricted resolutions and aspect ratios. Unlike traditional methods that
perceive images as static-resolution grids, FiT conceptualizes images as
sequences of dynamically-sized tokens. This perspective enables a flexible
training strategy that effortlessly adapts to diverse aspect ratios during both
training and inference phases, thus promoting resolution generalization and
eliminating biases induced by image cropping. Enhanced by a meticulously
adjusted network structure and the integration of training-free extrapolation
techniques, FiT exhibits remarkable flexibility in resolution extrapolation
generation. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate the exceptional performance
of FiT across a broad range of resolutions, showcasing its effectiveness both
within and beyond its training resolution distribution. Repository available at
https://github.com/whlzy/FiT.
add_method_texts.main_contributions: The paper introduces Flexible Vision Transformer (FiT), a novel transformer architecture for diffusion models capable of generating images at arbitrary resolutions and aspect ratios. FiT addresses the limitations of existing diffusion models like DiT, which struggle with generalizing across varying resolutions, by conceptualizing images as sequences of dynamically-sized tokens. Key contributions include a flexible training pipeline, a unique transformer architecture for dynamic token length modeling, and a training-free resolution extrapolation method.
add_method_texts.methodology: FiT utilizes a flexible training pipeline that preserves the original image aspect ratio by viewing the image as a sequence of tokens and adaptively resizing high-resolution images to fit within a predefined maximum token limit. The architecture incorporates 2D Rotary Positional Embedding (RoPE), Swish-Gated Linear Unit (SwiGLU) instead of traditional MLP, and Masked MHSA to efficiently manage padding tokens. Training-free extrapolation techniques, specifically VisionNTK and VisionYaRN, are tailored for 2D RoPE to enhance FiT's performance across various resolutions.
add_method_texts.experimental_setup: The model was trained on the ImageNet dataset with a maximum resolution limitation of HW <= 256^2. The performance was evaluated using metrics such as Fre'chet Inception Distance (FID), sFID, Inception Score (IS), and improved Precision and Recall. Experiments were conducted on different aspect ratios (1:1, 1:2, and 1:3) and resolutions, both within and out of the training distribution, to assess image synthesis and resolution extrapolation abilities.
add_method_texts.limitations: The FiT-XL/2 model was trained for a limited number of steps (1.8M), resulting in slightly inferior performance compared to DiT-XL/2 at the training resolution of 256x256. The generative capabilities of FiT-XL/2 were not thoroughly explored with higher resolution training (larger token length limitation). The research focused primarily on training-free resolution extrapolation techniques, without exploring methods that require additional training.
add_method_texts.future_research_directions: Future research directions include exploring the generative capabilities of FiT with higher resolution training, investigating resolution extrapolation methods that require additional training, and conducting further studies on generating images with arbitrary resolutions and aspect ratios using the FiT architecture.
